section: Center field: batter's eye (and Memory Lane behind it)

reference: img/cfwall.jpg and img/cf_full.jpg (Commons 'Center Field Wall at Citizens Bank Park (2372251698)', April 2008): three overlapping flat terracotta-brick walls, the main one rising ~2.5-3 m above the Alley walk, three separate ivy masses climbing it from a bed of rounded boxwood/juniper behind the 6 ft fence; the brick runs from behind the 409 corner past 401 to ~80% of the way to the 398 corner, and the bullpens only fill the last gap. hesb/2986448333.jpg (crop audit4/cr/ref-ws-cf.png) and hesb/2987306412.jpg (2008 World Series nights, from behind home): the same brick block with two big ivy masses, lit by the banks; only the upper half of the Alley storefronts shows above it. hesb/2986444537.jpg (2008 WS): English ivy leaves and shrubs close up. andrewclem.com/Baseball/CitizensBankPark.html: 'Three overlapping brick walls serve as the batter's eye in center field, and on the reverse side of them is a gallery of images from Philadelphia's baseball history'; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn_Alley: 'Memory Lane, located directly behind the batter's eye'. Confidence: high on form and materials, medium on the exact heights (from photo scale).
problem: Landmarks._battersEye() only lines the pit wall from 387 to 401 with an ivy-noise quad from y=0 to STREET (7.0 m) plus cone shrubs, so its top is flush with the concourse. From home plate, the mound and the high TV camera the whole Alley facade shows through as the hitter's background: Chickie's, Campo's and Planet Hoagie signs, the grey stand fronts, the Ashburn statue on its black plinth in the gap between the buildings. The 'eye' itself is a dark green strip (mean sRGB 26,51,38 by day) and pure black at night. It also stops at 401: the pens fill the whole 401-398 run where 2008 had brick. From the Alley the batter's eye doesn't exist. An open concrete plaza runs to the edge (e-behindBE), with no wall and no Memory Lane.
target: Three overlapping brick walls stepping up toward center: left step ~STREET+0.9 m (about 7.9 m above the field), main wall ~STREET+2.8 m (about 9.8 m), a set-back right wall ~STREET+2.2 m; spanning from behind the 409 corner (-5 deg) to about +8 deg (80% of the way 401->398). Brick salmon-terracotta: sunlit photo mean sRGB (207,146,128), so albedo about #9C5A48, light mortar #B9ADA0, vertical control joints every ~4.5 m, a 0.3 m cast-stone cap #C8B8A0. Ivy: three free-form masses covering ~55% of the face, each 6-9 m wide with ragged tops 1-3 m below the cap, leaf albedo #3F5A2C to #6E7C48 with lighter sunlit tips. Shrub bed of rounded boxwood/juniper 1.2-2.5 m high (#3E4A2A). Back face in the Alley: 'Memory Lane', a run of ~2 x 1.6 m illustrated history panels (Phillies, Athletics, Negro League teams) with small hood lights.
fix: Landmarks._battersEye(): replace the ivy quad with 3 extruded brick slabs (0.6 m thick) along offsetPolyline(this.bowl._fenceLine(...), 7) spanning fencePoint angles -5..+8 deg at the heights above, using the Alley brick shader (world-space u along the wall, keep the fr/fb far-fade) and a cap box; colliders via addBox (solid). Ivy: in the same shader, 3 hand-placed ellipse masks (x0, width, topY) broken up by mx_noise_float2(P*0.8) thresholded at 0.45; inside the mask output leaf albedo with a 0.25 m leaf-cluster normal pattern and AO toward the brick; add 150-250 alpha-tested leaf cards per mass along the ragged top and side edges (the card method from H30) so the silhouette isn't a straight line. Shrubs: SphereGeometry(1, 12, 8) scaled (1.2, 0.8, 1.2) clumps instead of stacked cones. Alley side: 12-16 'Memory Lane' panels (canvas 512x384, sepia photo + caption, drawn like the banner canvas) on the back face at STREET+1.0..2.6 m, each with a small hood lamp (emissive 0.6 at night). Shrink the bullpen span to match (see CR05).

reference: img/rf2.jpg (April 2008, from right-center toward the RF pole): the upper deck (McDonald's, AutoTrader boards) and the Pavilion (Chrysler/Jeep 'GREAT RUN HOME' board, Bud Light) run on behind the pole into the first-base 200/300 decks (MasterCard, LG, AIG boards, the 'WELCOME TO CITIZENS BANK PARK' ribbon) under one continuous truss roof. hesb/2987306412.jpg (2008 WS night, high behind home): the RF pole stands against an unbroken wall of fans on every level, McDonald's on the RF upper-deck fascia, 'DRINKABILITY' (Bud Light) on the Pavilion. img/rf1.jpg: the Pavilion front ads. audit2 G02 reported this gap and it is still open (it isn't in audit3/ranked.md).
problem: Bowl._buildUpperDecks() builds the Pavilion and Pavilion Deck on pavFront (the RF wall from 369 to 97% of the way to the pole), offset rfTop+1 m and +4 m. The Terrace 300/400 start from FOUL_TERRITORY[0] offset ~28 m back. Nothing fills the wedge between their ends, so from home plate, the 1B line and right field you see 30-40 m of sky, the rear parking and buildings and a low fan of field-level seats, with the Pavilion ending in a sheer grey slab. The Pavilion and Pavilion Deck fronts are plain light-grey bands with bunting; the Toyota/pitch-speed/Budweiser/Bud Light boards sit lower, on the back of the RF seats.
target: Continuous two-deck wrap round the RF pole: the Pavilion (200s, 12 rows) joins the first-base suite/Hall of Fame level and the Pavilion Deck joins the Terrace 300/400, with one roofline (standing-seam roof on trusses) running on past the pole. The pole stands in front of fans on every level. 2008 fascia boards: on the Pavilion front the Chrysler/Jeep 'GREAT RUN HOME' static board (~12 x 4 m, sky gradient, red Sebring convertible and green Wrangler), 'Bud Light'/'DRINKABILITY' (~6 x 2.5 m, navy), and TOYOTA + FAST BALL PITCH SPEED. On the upper-deck front, McDonald's (~9 x 1.5 m, red with yellow arches) and AutoTrader.com (orange/black).
fix: Bowl._buildUpperDecks(): add an 'rf-corner' fan tier at each upper level, like the lower bowl's corner() helper. Centre it on fencePoint(45, 330) and sweep from the Pavilion's end normal to the first Terrace segment's normal. Rows take the y0/rise of the tiers they join (pavilion to club-level/suite-seats, pavilion-deck to terrace-300 and terrace-400). Run _roof() along a polyline (Pavilion roof -> corner arc -> Terrace roof) so the roofline is continuous; _columns() under the fan. The simpler option: extend pavFront past the pole with a mitred corner and start the Terrace path from that corner point instead of FOUL_TERRITORY[0]. Remove the grey end slabs. Fascia.js: add _pavilionDeck(t) with McDonald's/AutoTrader in the ad atlas, and move the Chrysler/Jeep board (new canvas) and a Bud Light 'DRINKABILITY' board onto the Pavilion front at t.base-0.55.

section: Ashburn Alley architecture: storefront level, roof deck, retired numbers, clock

reference: img/cfwall.jpg and img/cf_full.jpg (April 2008): the storefront level (Tony Luke's, Seasons Pizza, Rick's Steaks, Brewerytown) is one storey (~4.5 m) under a maroon steel deck edge. Above it is an open roof deck with a galvanized picket rail lined with standing fans, lamp poles carrying the Ashburn banners, and a steel stair up at the right-center end. The two small brick houses with the retired numbers stand ON that deck either side of the clock, which sits on its own maroon steel frame over a brick pier. cbpimg/z_nums_left.jpg: red numerals about 40% of the house height with a thin white edge, names on small red plates in white capitals, black gooseneck barn lamps, a maroon door. img/flags.jpg: red and white Phillies patio umbrellas on the deck. andrewclem.com: 'fans on a budget can watch the game from the roof above the concession building beyond center field... plenty of standing room'. Clock sign: hesb/2986448333.jpg (crop audit4/cr/ref-ws-clock1.png) and hesb/2987306412.jpg (crop ref-ws-clock2.png), two 2008 World Series nights, show a lit BLUE rectangular box sign with white lettering under the clock, reading as Sherwin-Williams. The April 2008 photos show the MAB PAINTS oval, so it was changed during 2008. This reverses audit2 G05 for October; about 75% sure of the wording, sure of the blue rectangle.
problem: Landmarks._ashburnAlley(): each block is BoxGeometry(w, 8.5, 7.5) of brick with a trim cornice and a single 8 cm rail bar at +9.6 m. The stand signs sit at +3.25..4.65 m, leaving a 4 m blank brick band above them, the biggest single element of the CF backdrop from home. The number houses (16 x 5.2 m) sit on those roofs, so the numerals are 14-19 m above the field and oversized: they fill ~60% of the house height, with the names on bright white slabs. There's no roof deck: no picket rail, no lamp poles or banners up top, no stair, no umbrellas, and the flags stand on a bare roof. The clock sits on a squat brick box with the red MAB Paints oval.
target: Storefront level 4.5 m from the Alley floor to the deck. Deck edge: a 0.6 m maroon steel fascia beam (#5A1F1E) with a 1.07 m galvanized picket rail (#A7AAAD, pickets every 10 cm, 5 cm top rail). Lamp poles every ~12 m on the deck edge carry the pair of sepia Ashburn banners and a flood head. A steel stair (maroon stringers, galvanized rails) climbs at the right-center end, and 8-10 patio tables stand under red/white Phillies umbrellas. Number houses about 12 x 4.5 x 5 m on the deck: numerals 1.3 m, red #C8102E with a 3 cm white edge (42 in blue #1D3F8F), names on 1.6 x 0.3 m red plates in 0.18 m white capitals, a black barn lamp (0.5 m shade) over each number, a maroon door. Clock: a white face with a navy square ring and white bars on the maroon steel frame over a brick pier, with a blue (#0B4EA2) backlit Sherwin-Williams box sign (~4.5 x 0.8 m) under it for October 2008.
fix: Landmarks._ashburnAlley(): Hb 8.5 -> 4.5 for the storefront blocks (the colliders, the number houses' by and the rooftop bleachers' y0 all follow STREET+Hb). Replace the cornice with a deck-edge beam (box 0.6 m, this.steel) and build the rail with the rooftop bleachers' guard() helper in a new galvanized material (color 0.42/0.43/0.44, metalness 0.8, roughness 0.35) along zBack+D for every block. Move the banner lamp poles from the Alley floor to the deck edge (reuse the pole/banner Quads at y=STREET+Hb). Make the roofs walkable (colliders walkable:true) and add a stair at x~58 (beam() stringers + box treads). Number houses: bw 16->12, bh 5.2->4.5; on the 1536x512 canvas set the numeral font 300->180 px with an 8 px white strokeText, and draw the name plates red with white text. Add 3 gooseneck lamps per house (TubeGeometry arm + ConeGeometry shade with an emissive underside at night). _clock(): replace the 'mabPaints' canvas with a blue box sign (#0b4ea2 fill, white 'SHERWIN-WILLIAMS' 700 110px, emissive at night) sized 4.5 x 0.8 m. Umbrellas: ConeGeometry(1.2, 0.5, 8) canopies with a red/white stripe canvas on thin poles.

section: Right-center: the Liberty Bell sign and its tower
title: The Liberty Bell is a lamp-shade outline with a bar for a yoke on a thin mast; it has no castellated neon yoke, star lamps or heavy tower, and it doesn't swing at the final out
seen_in: audit4/cr/d-bell.png (http://127.0.0.1:5193/?hour=13&weather=off, __look(0,1.7,-20,53,44,-139,22)); audit4/cr/d-bellUnder.png (http://127.0.0.1:5193/?hour=13&weather=off, __look(40,8.7,-130,53,40,-139,65)); audit4/cr/n-bell.png (http://127.0.0.1:5193/?hour=21&weather=off, same __look as d-bell); audit4/cr/n-celbell.png (http://127.0.0.1:5193/?hour=21&weather=off, __cel(4) with the high camera: the bell is static during the title celebration); audit4/cr/d-homerf.png (http://127.0.0.1:5193/?hour=13&weather=off, __look(2,1.7,3,55,8,-85,40)). steps [{"file":"cam.js"},{"file":"audit3/seg.js"},{"js":"__start()","wait":1500},{"js":"__clean()"},{"js":"__look(...)","wait":2500},{"shot":...}]
reference: img/bell.jpg (April 2008 close-up): the bell outline is a white box channel carrying two parallel neon tubes; above it the yoke is a separate stepped (castellated) outline, wider than the shoulder, with a row of 5 star lamps. Inside the bell is a diagonal diamond lattice with ~20 eight-point star lamps on its nodes. The crack is an outlined zig-zag ribbon from the lip to the waist, and a medallion clapper with a star hangs under the lip. The sign hangs on the FRONT face of a heavy maroon lattice tower (~6 m wide, 4 legs, a caged ladder, 2 catwalk platforms) that carries on up behind the yoke. Below it on the same tower are the green Citizens Bank logo (8 arrowheads pointing in round a centre) and green channel letters. audit4/cr/ref-ws-bell.png (crop of hesb/2986448333.jpg, 2008 WS night): cool-white, slightly blue neon outline; the yoke outline with its star row is lit; the lattice is faintly lit; the crack is blue-white; the logo and 'Citizens Bank / Park' glow bright green in the bank's humanist sans with no white outline. ballparksofbaseball.com: 'Towering 50 feet high and 35 feet wide, the bell swings and lights up after every Phillies home run... 100 feet above street level... neon edges pulsate'. starlite.com (Citizens Bank Park projects): it 'lights up and swings after Philadelphia Phillies home runs and wins'. Extends audit F13 and audit2 G30, which were only partly done; neither is in audit3/ranked.md.
problem: Landmarks._libertyBell(): one profile (half[]) is traced 3 times by thin TubeGeometry (r=0.2) into a closed lamp-shade shape, filled with an orthogonal lattice (horizontal every 1.3 m, vertical every 1.4 m), a squiggle crack tube and a white ball clapper. The yoke is a solid maroon bar, which vanishes at night, so the night silhouette has no top. The bell balances on a slim 3.4 m lattice mast, and a separate wide X-braced frame carries 'Citizens Bank / Park' in bold Helvetica with a white stroke and a disc-with-star logo. Nothing animates when the Phillies win the Series.
target: Sign 15.8 m tall including the yoke and 10.7 m wide, lip ~31 m above the street. Outline: two parallel emissive tubes (r 0.08 m, 0.35 m apart) inside a white sheet-metal channel 0.5 m deep (#E8E8E4). Yoke: a stepped outline 11.5 x 3.2 m with 5 star lamps along its beam. Lattice: diamonds at +/-60 deg with 18-22 eight-point star lamps (0.6 m). Crack: an outlined zig-zag ribbon 0.5 m wide. Clapper: a 1.2 m medallion outline with a star. Neon cool white #E8F0FF (a touch bluer at night), stars warm white. Tower: maroon #5A1F1E, 6 x 4 m on 4 legs (0.35 m W-sections) with K-bracing every 3 m, a caged ladder and 2 catwalks with rails, rising from behind the rooftop bleachers to ~2 m above the yoke. Logo: Citizens green (#00A651, neon #2EE08A), an 8-chevron asterisk ~3 m across above 'Citizens Bank' / 'Park' channel letters (~2 m capitals, green faces, no white outline), mounted on the tower face.
fix: Rewrite _libertyBell(). (1) Outline: define the silhouette as 2D polylines in sign space (bell body, separate castellated yoke polygon, crack ribbon, clapper circle); sweep a rectangular channel along each (Quads side walls 0.5 m deep, white steel) with 2 inset TubeGeometry neon tubes per edge. (2) Lattice: beams at +/-60 deg clipped to the body with widthAt(), and an InstancedMesh of flat 8-point star quads with emissive at the intersections. (3) Tower: a non-square variant of lattice() (6 x 4 m), catwalk platforms at y0-2 and y0+H, a ladder (2 rails + rungs every 0.3 m); mount the sign at local z=-0.8 on the front face and delete the separate fq frame. (4) Letters: redraw the canvas in a humanist sans ('Frutiger', 'Myriad Pro', 'Segoe UI', sans-serif, weight 600) with no white stroke, green #1FA65A albedo and #2EE08A x2.2 emissive at night; draw the logo as 8 chevrons rotated in 45 deg steps round a hole of radius 0.25. (5) Swing: put body + crack + clapper + lattice in a child Group pivoted at the yoke (y0+0.93H). In update(), when the Director reaches a Phillies HR or the 'celebrate' segment, set rotation.z = 0.18*sin(2*pi*0.55*t)*exp(-t/6) for ~12 s, chase the neon (emissive *= 0.6+0.4*step(fract(uv.x*0.5 - t*2), 0.5) along the tube u) and flash the stars; play a bell 'dong' sample every 1.8 s, positioned at the sign.

reference: hesb/2986444537.jpg (2008 World Series). The lower (Phillies) pen is a recess under the upper pen's front: ~2.4 m clear under a teal-grey soffit, a long brown slat bench with relievers in red jackets, an orange Gatorade cooler on a red stand, a propane torpedo heater, folding chairs and a white bullpen box. The upper (visitors') pen front is a teal concrete lip with window boxes of purple, pink and white petunias and trailing ivy, behind a galvanized square-post rail with chain-link panels (~1.2 m). The CF fence rail in front is padded teal. img/cfwall.jpg (April 2008): the Wall of Fame is 2 rows of bronze plaques on RED BRICK at Alley level, left of the upper pen. The pens show only in the last ~20% of the 401-398 run and carry on behind the RF seats' wedge. andrewclem.com: 'The bullpens are situated behind the wedge-shaped extremity of the right-center field lower deck, and partly covered by the second deck'. baseballparks.com: Phillies in the lower pen, visitors in the upper one beside the concourse. img/wof.jpg: 33 plaques (relief portrait + text, ~0.55 x 0.85 m) plus the wider 'Phillies Centennial Team' plaque.
problem: Field._buildBullpens() 'pen-chain-link' shader: alpha = max(step(0.42 - fw, max(g.x,g.y))*step(fw,0.9), clamp(fw*0.35,0,0.35)). Once fwidth(p.x) > 0.42 (past ~15 m, or at a grazing angle from the Alley) the step() term is 1 for EVERY pixel, so the 2.2 m band over the fence and the 1.4 m band on the upper-pen lip render as solid dark-green or black sheets. From the field the pens are hidden behind a blank 4 m wall; from the Alley they sit behind black wedges. The lower pen is open, sky-lit grass with a 7 m shelter at its far end, so there's no bench recess or gear to see through the fence. The mums planter is large-scale purple and white noise that reads as camouflage. The Wall of Fame is 40 flat brown boxes on the teal pen wall.
target: Chain-link reads as a faint grey veil at distance (~15-25% coverage), never solid. The lower pen is a lit recess with the bench, cooler, heater and chairs visible through the fence. The upper-pen lip carries flower window boxes and a galvanized rail. Wall of Fame: 2 rows of 17 bronze plaques (0.55 x 0.85 m, #6B4A2B with lighter relief portraits) plus the 1.8 m Centennial Team plaque, on brick (#9C5A48) at Alley level.
fix: (1) Chain-link, and the same pattern in the foul-pole screen (CR10): wire = 1 - smoothstep(0.42 - fw, 0.42, max(g.x, g.y)); alpha = mix(wire, 0.18, saturate(fw*1.5)), then use a dithered alpha test (alpha > hash(fragCoord.xy)) or alpha-to-coverage so distant mesh is 18% dark instead of solid. (2) Lower pen as a recess: a soffit slab over its back 3 m at y=2.4 (#3B5552), a 14 m slat bench (box per slat, #6B4A30), an orange cooler on a red stand, a torpedo heater, 3 folding chairs, and 2 linear fixtures (emissive 1.2 at night). Drop the separate lower shelter. (3) Upper-pen lip: 0.3 x 0.3 m window boxes filled with alpha-tested flower cards (0.15 m clusters, purple #7A3FA0, pink #D05A9A, white) and trailing ivy cards, replacing the noise planter; a galvanized rail with chain-link panels. (4) Span: start the pens where CR01's brick ends (~+8 deg) and run them past the 398 corner, behind the RF seats' wedge, with the upper pen partly under the RF seats/Pavilion overhang. (5) Details2008._wallOfFame(): move the plaques to a brick parapet at Alley level (STREET-1.9..STREET) facing the field at the left end of the upper pen, 2 x 17 plaques from a canvas atlas (sepia-bronze relief portrait + 8 text lines each) plus one 1.8 x 0.85 m Centennial plaque; metalness 0.85, roughness 0.35, darker patina in the text area.

The clock face is lit white with the blue sign under it, and the Liberty Bell and green letters are the brightest things in right-center. hesb/2987305440.jpg (crop audit4/cr/ref-night-cf.png): the same from the 3B upper deck.
problem: In n-clock the batter's-eye hedge is pure black and the brick buildings are dark maroon; the retired numerals are barely legible because nothing lights them. The stand signs are dim (alley-signs emissive mix(0.2, 0.6, night)) under dark canopies, and apart from the lamp discs no warm light spills onto the Alley floor or the facades. Only the clock and the flags pop. From home and the high camera the whole CF strip is a dark band between the lit field and the black sky, where 2008 TV showed a warm, busy, lit backdrop.
target: Field-facing brick in CF at ~35-50% of its daytime luminance, lit by spill from the banks. Alley signs at ~150-300 nits, the brightest band after the bell and the scoreboard. A warm 3000-3500 K glow from the counters spilling 3-5 m onto the floor. Retired numbers washed by their gooseneck lamps (a pool on the brick under each), deck lamps lit, flags floodlit as now.
fix: (1) Spill: the banks are the night key (H02 adds per-bank shadows for players). For static geometry in CF add a cheap 'bank spill' term to the brick, ivy and Alley materials: for each bank position (the roof and tower banks from Bowl._lightTower / the night lighting setup) add bankColor * I * max(dot(N, L), 0) / (1 + d*d/120^2), unshadowed, with I set so field-facing brick reaches linear L ~0.12. Or add 2 wide spot lights from the RF/LF roof banks aimed at the CF wall. (2) alley-signs emissive mix(0.2, 1.6, frame.night), and bloom on. (3) Retired numbers: 3 gooseneck lamps per house (CR03), plus a light pool computed in the brick shader: e += vec3(1.0, 0.8, 0.55) * 0.8 * exp(-dist2(P, lampPos)/1.44) for the 6 lamp positions passed as a uniform array. (4) alley-floor shader: radial warm pools (radius 4 m) under each lamp pole and in front of each counter, scaled by frame.night.

A green Citizens Bank ATM kiosk and red and yellow carts stand along the walk. img/bulls.jpg: red brick pavers with a concrete band, red picnic tables, red/white umbrellas, red trash cans with the Phillies logo, grey single-disc lamp posts. img/pennants.jpg: the banner poles with pennant flags over the walk. en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn_Alley: a 'street-fair' promenade 625 ft long with the All-Star Walk granite markers, the Alley Store, the Citizens Bank 'Games of Baseball' and 'a 22-foot baseball-themed pinball machine operated here before 2010'; ballparksofbaseball.com: 625 ft, 50,000 sq ft, picnic areas.
problem: From Alley eye level ~50% of the frame is a flat concrete plain (the 8.5 m alley-floor quad plus the concourse slab that runs on over the pit edge to the RF seats). The field edge is a bare drop with no rail, fans' leaning bar, flower boxes or signage. The only furniture is lamp posts and three picnic tables. H10 already asks for brick pavers, a railing and the All-Star plaques. What it doesn't cover: the rail should be galvanized silver, not green; the walk should be bounded by the batter's-eye wall (CR01); and the street-fair clutter that made the 2008 Alley busy even before the crowd arrives is missing.
target: A ~12-15 m wide brick promenade. On the field side: the Memory Lane wall behind the batter's eye, then a 1.07 m galvanized picket rail (#A7AAAD) with green window boxes over the pens and in left-center. Along the walk: the Games of Baseball booth (Citizens green/white), the 22 ft pinball cabinet, the Alley Store front, the green Citizens Bank ATM kiosk, 2-3 carts (red/yellow awnings), red Phillies trash and recycling cans every ~15 m, and picnic tables with red/white umbrellas at both ends. Granite All-Star Walk markers (0.6 x 0.6 m) in the floor.
fix: Landmarks._alleyLife(): add a field-edge rail along the pit outline between the batter's eye and the RF seats using the rooftop bleachers' guard() helper in a galvanized material, with 0.9 m green window boxes (box + flower cards, CR05) every 2.4 m. Scatter props from a small kit in geo.js style boxes (all in Quads batches): ATM kiosk (1.2 x 0.8 x 2.2 m, #00A651 with a white Citizens logo canvas), carts (2 x 1 m, awning quad), trash cans (CylinderGeometry(0.3, 0.3, 0.9) red #B01E2A with a Phillies decal), a 7 m pinball cabinet (tilted playfield box + backbox with a canvas), and a Games of Baseball booth (3 x 3 m frame with net). Place 12 granite markers as floor decals in the alley-floor shader (a grid mask every 6 m, #7E7C78, a thin engraved-text noise). Clip the concourse slab behind the Alley so the walk reads as a promenade and not an apron.

reference: img/rfpole.jpg (April 2008, the RF pole from the RF seats): a plain round yellow pole about 0.45 m in diameter (judged against fans' heads), with no screen on its lower half; sampled sRGB (212,193,98) in sun. img/lfpole.jpg (the LF pole, same design): a plain round pole up past the upper deck, with a yellow stripe down the wall padding under it. hesb/2987306412.jpg (2008 WS night, high behind home): both poles read as thin bright yellow lines.
problem: Field._buildFoulPoles(): the pole (r 0.18-0.24 m) is right, but a 0.9 m wire screen runs from 4 m to the top. Its shader sets alpha = max(wire, clamp(fw*0.8, 0, 0.55)) against alphaTest 0.5, so once fw > 0.625 the whole screen is opaque. At distance the pole plus screen becomes a ~1.3 m flat yellow panel with a lighter strip, three times wider than the 2008 photos and a plank in every TV shot. The colour (0.76, 0.6, 0.1) is fine.
target: A round pole 0.45-0.5 m in diameter, #E3CD4B painted steel, ~26 m tall, collar at the wall top and the yellow wall stripe as now. No screen on the lower two thirds; if kept at all, a mesh at most 0.4 m wide on the top 8 m that reads no more than 20% opaque at distance.
fix: Remove the screen, or shrink it to 0.4 m wide on the top 8 m and give its shader CR05's coverage/dithered alpha. Set the cylinder to r 0.23/0.25 m with 32 segments, roughness 0.45, metalness 0.2. Keep the collar and the wall stripe; the same change fixes the left field pole.
